title: Eyes on the chips: the seaside war between humans and gulls

sents.en: Across the world's beach towns, bold seabirds have learned that tourists are an easy meal.
sents.zh: 在世界各地的海滩小镇，胆大的海鸟已经摸清了：游客就是送上门的一顿饭。

sents.en: Scientists think they have found a surprisingly simple defence.
sents.zh: 科学家认为，他们找到了一个简单得出奇的防御办法。

sents.en: It happens in a flash.
sents.zh: 事情就发生在一眨眼之间。

sents.en: The children shriek, the parents shout, and the bird retreats to a rooftop to enjoy its prize.
sents.zh: 孩子们尖叫，大人们大喊，那只鸟则退到屋顶上享用它的战利品。

sents.en: Similar scenes play out every summer from Brighton to Sydney to Cape Town.
sents.zh: 从布莱顿到悉尼再到开普敦，每年夏天都在上演类似的场面。

sents.en: Gulls were not always this cheeky.
sents.zh: 海鸥并不是一直都这么厚脸皮。

sents.en: For most of their history they fed at sea, scavenging behind fishing boats and picking through the shoreline.
sents.zh: 在漫长的历史中，它们大多在海上觅食，跟在渔船后面捡食，在海岸边翻找吃的。

sents.en: But as fish stocks dwindled and towns filled up with litter, rubbish bins and outdoor diners, many birds moved inland and adapted with remarkable speed.
sents.zh: 可随着鱼类资源越来越少，镇上到处是垃圾、垃圾桶和露天吃饭的人，许多海鸥搬到了内陆，而且适应得快得惊人。

sents.en: A city gull can live for 20 years, remembers where food is easy to come by, and learns by watching other gulls get away with theft.
sents.zh: 一只城市海鸥能活二十年，记得哪里容易找到吃的，还会看着别的海鸥偷了东西没事，跟着学。

sents.en: Residents are at their wits' end.
sents.zh: 居民们已经无计可施了。

sents.en: Councils have tried everything from spiked roofs and fake owls to fines for anyone caught feeding the birds.
sents.zh: 地方政府什么办法都试过：从在屋顶装尖刺、摆假猫头鹰，到对被抓到喂鸟的人罚款。

sents.en: Some towns have hired falconers, whose hawks patrol the beach to scare gulls off.
sents.zh: 有些镇雇了驯鹰人，让他们的鹰在海滩上巡逻，把海鸥吓跑。

sents.en: Most of these measures work for a while; then the gulls catch on and come back.
sents.zh: 这些办法大多能管用一阵子，然后海鸥就看穿了，又回来了。

sents.en: Researchers studying gull behaviour have come up with a cheaper idea: stare them down.
sents.zh: 研究海鸥行为的研究人员想出了一个更省钱的办法：瞪着它们，直到它们退缩。

sents.en: In one experiment, scientists placed a bag of chips on the ground and watched how long passing gulls took to approach it.
sents.zh: 在一项实验里，科学家把一袋薯条放在地上，观察路过的海鸥要过多久才会靠近。

sents.en: When a person kept their eyes fixed on the bird, it hesitated far longer than when the person looked away, and many gave up altogether.
sents.zh: 如果人一直盯着鸟看，它犹豫的时间比人把目光移开时长得多，很多干脆放弃了。

sents.en: Gulls, it seems, are wary of being watched, perhaps because a staring animal is more likely to fight back.
sents.zh: 看来，海鸥不喜欢被人盯着，也许是因为一个瞪着你的动物更可能会反击。

sents.en: There is a catch, of course.
sents.zh: 当然，这里面也有个问题。

sents.en: Only a minority of the gulls dared to come near the food, and the boldest barely paused before grabbing it.
sents.zh: 只有少数海鸥敢靠近食物，而胆子最大的那几只几乎不停顿就抢走了。

sents.en: And it is hard to keep an eye on a gull while also eating, chatting and keeping track of small children.
sents.zh: 而且一边吃东西、聊天、看着小孩，一边还要盯住一只海鸥，实在不容易。

sents.en: Still, the finding hints at something that frustrated towns often miss.
sents.zh: 不过，这个发现指出了一点，焦头烂额的小镇常常忽略。

sents.en: Gulls are not villains; they are opportunists doing what any sensible animal would do when food is left lying around.
sents.zh: 海鸥并不是坏蛋；它们只是投机者，吃的东西随便放着的时候，任何聪明的动物都会这么做。

sents.en: Many species are in decline at sea even as their urban cousins thrive, which makes culling them hard to justify.
sents.zh: 许多种类的海鸥在海上数量正在减少，而它们城里的“亲戚”却过得很好，所以很难找到理由去捕杀它们。

sents.en: The best defence may simply be to eat indoors, keep bins closed and, when all else fails, look the bird in the eye.
sents.zh: 最好的防御办法也许就是：在室内吃饭，盖好垃圾桶，实在不行，就直视那只鸟的眼睛。

sents.en: It will not win the war, but it might save your lunch.
sents.zh: 这赢不了整场战争，但也许能保住你的午饭。
